Commentary.Commentary: Miguel Cummins and Jason Holder continued the good work and ensured that the lower order and the tail didn't wag. A lot of soul searching to do for the visitors. First of all, they would want to forget this as quickly as possible and get going with the ball. The Windies, on the other hand, would be aiming to continue the domination. Meanwhile, the groundsmen are bringing in the covers for precautionary purpose, in case it rains. Join us shortly!

What a dismal start to the tour for the visiting side as they have been bowled out for their lowest innings total in Test cricket! Agreed that the conditions were helpful for the pacers but the Bangladeshi batsmen couldn't come to terms with the pace and bounce of the track at all. It was Kemar Roach who broke the backbone of the opposition, nipping out five wickets in the first hour itself. He bowled nagging lines and lengths, induced false strokes and got the results.

OUT! Bowled 'em! That is the final nail in the coffin. Full length ball attacking the stumps, the ball moves away just a shade. Jayed exposes his stumps and sees them shattered. BANGLADESH ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 43!
Close shave! Back of a length ball on off, Jayed hops and tries to keep it out but gets an outside edge. The ball falls just short of the third slip fielder.
Full and outside off, Abu goes after it and is beaten.
Outside off, Jayed pushes at it and misses.

FOUR! Something to smile about for the visitors on a tough day! Cummins searches for the yorker but ends up overpitching it on middle. Hossain takes full toll of it as he drills it through mid on to find the fence. This is only the third boundary of the innings.
Length ball, angling in, Hossain in his customary manner backs away and tries to slog it over mid on but misses. The ball goes over the stumps to the keeper.
Another play and a miss from the tailender.
Pitched up delivery outside off, Hossain makes room and tries to go over covers but only connects with thin air.
Outside off, Jayed plays it towards point where the fielder doesn't collect it cleanly and concedes a single.
In the channel outside off, Abu leaves it alone.
Ouch! Good length ball on middle and leg, seaming in. Hossain backs away a touch and gets an inside edge near the box region.
Pitched up ball outside off, Hossain lofts it over covers for a couple.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball but fails.
Well played, young lad! Fullish ball on middle, Jayed leans ahead and taps it through mid on to pick up a couple.
The debutant, Abu Jayed comes out to bat.

OUT! A beauty to send the tailender packing! Captain Holder has delivered as well. He bends his back and bowls an effort ball around off. The ball takes off like a helicopter as Islam tries to ride it but an outside edge results. Dowrich takes it neatly.
Chin music! The tailender will be uncomfortable. Short ball on off, Islam ducks under it awkwardly.
Outside off, a poke and a miss.
Good length ball outside off, Hossain leaves it.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Rubel Hossain is the new man in.

OUT! The procession continues! Bangladesh will not like this one bit. They are now in danger of getting bowled out for their lowest total if they don't cross 62. Pitched up ball around off, a bit of nibble on it. Mehedi Hasan pushes at it tamely and gets a thick outside edge towards the slip cordon. The ball is dying on its way through and hence, Devon Smith at second slip takes a quick decision to go for the catch. He dives to his left and takes it inches above the ground. Seems like he has caught it but the umpire waits. However, the batsman continues to walk back. The replay shows that it was clean.
In the zone outside off, Mehedi lets it go.
On a good length outside off, holding its line. Hasan plays down the wrong line and misses.
Back of a length ball in the tight off stump corridor, shaping away after landing. Islam fiddles with it and is beaten.
Angling in sharply as Mehedi clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Full length ball, kept out watchfully.
Pitched up delivery, Hasan lunges in defense.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Outside off, Mehedi has a poke at it and misses.
Kamrul Islam Rabbi comes out to bat.

OUT! The sad story continues for the tourists! This on a full length on off, moves away late. Hasan is on the move in order to flick it through mid-wicket but gets a leading outside edge. Holder at third slip takes it and throws the ball up in joy!
Good length ball, answered with a straight bat.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.
Fullish ball, defended off the front foot.
Mehedi Hasan ambles out to bat.

OUT! Das' star has finally stopped shining! After playing and missing on countless occasions, he has finally fallen. After a couple of barren games, Cummins comes into the act. Coming back to the ball, it is on a fuller length on off. Das attempts an ugly loft across the line but only manages a leading edge. The ball skies over the point region. Roston Chase stationed in that region chases it to his right and takes a well-judged catch.
On a good length around off, kept out with a straight bat.
Extravagent movement! Swinging away late from around off, Nurul tries to cover the line with a shuffle but gets beaten.
Full ball outside off, Hasan chases it and gets beaten.
Holder hasn't found his mark yet! This is on the pads, clipped through mid-wicket for a couple.
Das continues to flirt with danger! Fuller in length on off, Das leans ahead and  lifts in unconvincingly over mid on. A couple taken.
Similar length ball, dabbed with an open bat face to the same region.
Shimron Hetmyer is the substitute fielder in place of Kemar Roach.
On a length outside off, played with an angled bat past point for a run.
Fullish ball around off, kept out watchfully.
It's been driven superbly through the covers. They manage to come back for the second.

FOUR! Poor shot selection! Shortish ball outside off, Das fetches it from there and mistimes his pull over mid-wicket. There is no one there and he picks up a boundary. If he would have departed on this one, would have looked really silly.
Back of a length around off, Das rises with the bounce and pokes at it but gets a thick outside edge towards gully.
Das is leading a charmed life! Seems like he is carrying a magic wand with him. Full and outside off, Das goes at it with minimal foot movement and is beaten all ends up.
Fullish ball on leg stump, tucked towards the man at backward square leg.
Miguel Cummins comes in for a burst.

Time for Drinks! There are things which you dream of as a team. This one has been fulfilled, courtesy Kemar Roach. The athletic pacer has been in beautiful rhythm from the word go and hasn't let his intensity drop even a bit. His figures read 5-1-8-5. He has literally ran through the opposition. On the contrary, Bangladesh have been in shambles. Minimal footwork, poking at deliveries which can be left alone and not learning from their mistakes have cost them dearly so far. It will require a herculean effort from them to come back into the contest.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, third leave in a row. Better from Das.
Good length ball outside off, holding its line. Liton points his bat skywards to let it through.
Length ball outside off, not fiddled with.
Erring in line, on the hips, tucked around the corner for a run.
In the zone outside off, left alone.
Jason Holder comes in as first change after a terrific spell from Kemar Roach.
Another play and a miss! The opener is not learning from his mistakes. Full ball outside off, late away movement on that. Das goes for an expansive push but misses.
Outside off, sanity prevails for Liton as he lets it go.
He tries to repeat the same shot to a similar ball and is beaten again.
With half the side back in the hut, this is an absolutely reckless shot! Outside off on a full length, Das goes for a booming drive but the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Fractionally overpitched, clipped through mid on for a couple.
Gabriel sprays this one way down the leg side as Dowrich has to dive full length to stop it.
Roach doesn't get the hat-trick! Sprays this one on the pads, clipped through mid-wicket for a brace. A terrific over though, 3 wickets and two runs from it.
Nurul Hasan strides out to bat. Roach is on a hat-trick. Can he get it?

OUT! Another one bites the dust! 8th Test fifer for Kemar Roach and he has broken the backbone of the tourists single-handedly. This was similar to the dismissal of Tamim Iqbal. On a good length on off, straightens after pitching. Mahumudullah tries to cover the line but can't. Ekes out an outside edge and Shane Dowrich behind the stumps takes a straightforward catch. The visitors are completely at sea.
Mahmudullah is the new man in.

OUT! This is going from bad to worse for Bangladesh! What a start for the Windies though. We are only 45 minutes into the game and the athletic pacer has exploited the conditions to the optimum. He bowls this one in the avenue of apprehension around off and gets the ball to straighten after landing. That is enough to induce an outside edge from the hanging bat of Shakib. Jason Holder at third slip is safe as a house and accepts it gleefully.
Fullish ball around off, pushed off the front foot to mid off.
The skipper, Shakib Al Hasan comes out to bat. He is returning to Test cricket after 9 months. Needs to play a captain's knock here.

OUT! The impact is fine! Bangladesh lose another experienced campaigner and are out of sorts at the moment. Third wicket for Roach! He goes wider of the crease and dishes out a fullish ball outside off. After pitching, it seams in as Rahim tries to keep it out but fails to do so and is pinged on the front pad. The Windies go up in unison and up goes the umpire's finger. Rahim has a look of anguish on his face and walks gingerly towards his partner. Decides to take the DRS eventually. Seems it will go waste though as it looked pretty adjacent. Time for the replays. The Hawk Eye rolls in and the impact is umpire's call. Then, the ball is going onto crash into the stumps. The on-field call stays. The visitors don't lose a review but they are in deep trouble.

Bangladesh are in deep, deep trouble! Roach has trapped Rahim in front of the stumps. However, the wicket-keeper batsman walks towards his partner and after a consultation, opts for the review. Only the impact is in question.
Outside off, Rahim doesn't play at it.
The third play and a miss in the over! Back of a length well outside off, there is no need to chase it but Das does just that only to miss it. He is flirting with danger.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
In the zone outside off, Liton lets it go.
This is poor from Das! Gabriel bowls this one on a full length wide outside off and he goes chasing after it. Luckily for him, he doesn't reach it or otherwise he would have been on his way back.
Beaten comprehensively! Back of a length around off, leaves Das after pitching. The batsman is opened up in his stance as he pokes at it and gets foxed.
Fullish ball around off, pushed through mid on for a brace.
Mushfiqur Rahim is the new man in. This is his 50th Test innings away from home and he will want to make it a memorable one. Meanwhile, Roach gets his right leg stretched from the physio.

OUT! Gone! Roach is amidst a beautiful spell and he has pushed Bangladesh on the back foot. In the previous series against Sri Lanka, Roach's 8 out of 11 wickets were left-handers and he has added a couple more to his tally. Coming back to the ball, it is on a fullish length outside off, luring Haque to attempt something ambitious. He falls for the bait and goes for a drive away from his body. The bad thing is that he is on the move as well and hence, in no control. Ends up getting a thick outside edge towards gully where Shai Hope takes a fine catch. Roach immediately clutches below his right knee in his followthrough. Seems to be in some pain.

Edgy! Good length ball around off, straightens after landing. Haque tries to defend but gets an outside edge which falls short of the slip cordon. The good thing was that he played it with soft hands.
Angling into Liton who tucks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Fullish delivery, kept out watchfully.

In the air... but just wide! Fullish delivery, tailing in nicely. Das falls over a bit in an attempt to flick it across the line and the bat also turns in his hands. Bishoo is on the move as he goes to his right but doesn't dive. Two runs is the result. Well, the replays indicate that he should have dived. The ball was not far from him. Such small things matter a lot in cricket. Need to be proactive throughout the game.
Haque is off the mark immediately! Slightly overpitched on off, played with soft hands to covers for a single.
Stump-to-stump line, blocked solidly off the back foot.

That good length area is causing problems for the batsmen. Credit to the hosts for exploiting the same. Around off, a lot of zip on that one and the ball moves away as well to catch Das off guard. That was inches away from the outside edge of his blade.
On a length outside off, Liton takes a stride forward and punches it on the up to the extra cover fielder.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Gabriel tests Das with a bouncer but he is up to it as he ducks under it.
Shortish ball on middle and off, Das pulls it unconvincingly past short leg and picks up a couple.
Mominul Haque comes in at No. 3.

OUT! Roach produces a beauty to give his side the initial breakthrough! He was continuously bowling a nagging line and length around the off stump corridor and has finally reaped the dividends. He bowls a good length ball around off from around the wicket, coming in with the natural angle. However, the ball just straightens a touch after landing. Iqbal has no option but to play at it and all he manages is a thin outside edge which is pouched safely by Shane Dowrich. Delight for the Windies!
Length ball well outside off, Iqbal is not tempted to fiddle with it.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

Signs that this track has good bounce! Roach bowls a short of a length ball around off and gets the ball to take off along with significant inward seam movement. Iqbal rises with the bounce and manages to block it towards short leg.

Full length ball, swinging in from outside off. Liton is once again a touch jittery. Doesn't commit himself on the front foot and hence, an inside edge is induced on the push. The ball rolls towards wide mid on and the batsmen take a run.
Length ball outside off, Das points his bat skywards to let it be.
Erring in line and length. It is on the pads as well as overpitched. Iqbal flicks it with soft hands through mid-wicket and takes a brace.

Close shave! Good use of the crease from Gabriel. He goes wide of the crease and bowls a length ball which angles in prodigiously. Das is on his toes as he leaves his bottom hand from the handle but gets it off the inner half past the short leg fielder. That was not far away from him. A run results.
Gabriel hits the deck hard this time and generates some good bounce outside off, Das hops and taps it to the point region.
Fourth stump line from Gabriel, Liton shuffles a touch and blocks it solidly.
Length ball around off, Liton camps back and answers it with a straight bat.
Change in the field. An extra man comes in the slip cordon, the fourth slip to be precise.
Composed! Fullish ball on off, Iqbal presses forward and dabs it to cover-point for a single.
Fuller in length around off, Liton puts his head down and defends it nicely.
That's a jaffa! On a good length outside off and after landing, the ball seams in with extra bounce. Das is in an uncomfortable position as he tries to block it and is beaten on the inside.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
A bit fuller in length in the tight off stump corridor, kept out watchfully.
Another play and a miss! In the corridor of uncertainty, the ball pitches and seams in. Das looks to cover the line but misses.
Tamim Iqbal is off the mark! On middle and leg, tucked to fine leg for a single.
Gabriel smartly swings this one away after bringing a couple in. Das fishes at it and is foxed. Brilliant start from Gabriel.
Shaping in substantially, Liton once again fails to counter the movement. The ball hits his pads and lobs past the short leg fielder towards square leg.
This is good bowling! Gabriel goes wider of the crease and angles in a length ball. Das is bamboozled by the sharp movement as he gets beaten and is struck on the thigh pads.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! Ooh! Just wide of the diving gully fielder! Streaky runs. In the avenue of apprehension, straightens a bit after landing. Liton Das pokes at it with zero feet movement and gets a thick outside edge. The ball just goes past the left side of Hope and races to the fence.
Aggression from Gabriel immediately! Seems he is nicely worked up. He steams in and bowls a bouncer around leg stump, Das ducks under it in a jiffy.
Shannon Gabriel to share the new ball from the other end.

Tentative! On a length around off, there is a bit of nibble in the air. Iqbal is unsure whether to come forward or stay back. Ends up getting into a bit of tangle but the inside edge on his pads saves him. A maiden from Roach to start with!
Nicely played eventually! In the tight off stump corridor, Iqbal comes half-forward and plays it with soft hands. Gets it off the outer half of the bat towards third slip.
A touch fuller in length but this one swings away. It is well outside off and hence, Iqbal isn't forced into a false stroke.
Well bowled! On a length in the corridor of uncertainty, shaping in sharply. Tamim keeps his bat inside the line and lets it go.
Similar delivery, coming in with the natural angle, Tamim is solid in his defense.
On the money to begin with! Roach steams in from around the wicket and attacks the stumps with a full ball. Iqbal leans ahead and blocks it right under his eyes.

We are set to get underway as the slight drizzle has fizzed off. Good news for everyone! Tamim Iqbal and Liton Das will open the batting for Bangladesh. Kemar Roach will start the proceedings with the brand new cherry. Three slips, a gully and a short leg in position. Here we go...

Shakib Al Hasan says that it will be a tough series for them but their preparation is good. States that he is happy with his team and it will come down to how they perform. Ends by saying that they are going in with three pacers and two spinners.

Jason Holder says that they will bowl first. Feels that there is a bit of moisture on it and he will want his pacers to make use of it. Mentions they need to be consistent and sort out their no ball issues.
TOSS - The Windies win the toss and opt to field.

PITCH REPORT - Jeff Dujon assessing the surface says that there is a tinge of green on it but it has been rolled in as well. Feels that it will be tough for the batsmen initially. Reckons that it is a bowl first wicket.

Bangladesh, on the other hand, need to rise up to the occasion. They are a much-improved team, especially in limited-overs cricket but they need to translate such performances in the longest format of the game as well. Shakib Al Hasan is returning after a hiatus of 9 months in Test cricket and he will be a vital cog in the wheel for the visitors, both with bat and ball. Expect a cracker!

Overcast skies welcome us in Antigua, something which will please the pace bowlers. Cricket has taken center-stage in the Caribbean once again and it promises to be an exciting contest between two nations who have some formidable players in the mix. The hosts will be happy with the fact that their pace battery is well-oiled at the moment but they will be hoping for more consistent performances from their batsmen. Jason Holder has been leading from the front and will be aiming to inspire his men.
